Requesting changes because this currently forwards an ambiguous path/URI across the Gateway-to-node boundary without defining who owns the bytes.

Blocking findings:

1. `media://inbound/...` is Gateway-managed input. Forwarding it unchanged asks the remote node to resolve the same opaque URI against a different inbound store, which can fail or select unrelated node-local state.
2. The success test uses `/home/node-user/uploads/report.pdf`, but the real node upload route only accepts its managed upload root or node inbound media. The mocked `node.invoke` proves forwarding, not that the real route accepts the path.
3. The `media://inbound/node-only-file.pdf` test succeeds only because the node proxy is mocked; that URI is explicitly Gateway-owned in the browser tool context.
4. The sibling browser CLI still resolves files on the Gateway before `/hooks/file-chooser`, so this is a one-sided fix for a shared upload contract.
5. Automatic host fallback can switch an auto-selected node request back to the Gateway, making raw-source semantics depend on routing outcome.

Best-fix verdict: wrong layer. Define an explicit source-ownership/transport contract. Gateway-managed bytes should be staged into the node-managed upload root with cleanup, following the lifecycle pattern in `src/infra/terminal-file-upload.ts`. Truly node-local sources need a distinct explicit input shape. Apply the same contract to the tool and CLI paths, then prove it against a real remote browser node.

Issue remains open: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/115251
